events.title: Xia Dynasty Founded
events.description: The Xia Dynasty, traditionally considered China's first hereditary dynasty, was established by Yu the Great after his successful flood control efforts. Though archaeological evidence remains under research, the Xia Dynasty holds an important place in Chinese historical tradition as a foundational civilization.

events.title: Shang Dynasty Established
events.description: Tang of Shang overthrew the Xia and established the Shang Dynasty. The Shang is the first Chinese dynasty with direct written records and archaeological evidence, famous for oracle bone script which laid the foundation for Chinese writing. Bronze casting reached its peak during this period.

events.title: Zhou Dynasty Founded
events.description: King Wu of Zhou defeated the Shang and established the Zhou Dynasty, implementing feudalism and clan systems. The Zhou introduced the 'Mandate of Heaven' concept, establishing philosophical foundations for Chinese governance. The dynasty lasted approximately 800 years, divided into Western and Eastern Zhou periods.

events.title: Eastern Zhou Begins (Spring and Autumn Period)
events.description: King Ping moved the capital east to Luoyi, marking the start of Eastern Zhou. The Spring and Autumn period saw various lords competing for hegemony. Confucianism and Taoism began to emerge, laying groundwork for the Hundred Schools of Thought.

events.title: Birth of Confucius
events.description: Confucius, founder of Confucianism, was born in the State of Lu. He promoted concepts of 'benevolence' and 'propriety,' emphasizing education and moral cultivation. His philosophy profoundly influenced Chinese and East Asian culture for over two millennia.

events.title: Warring States Period Begins
events.description: The Spring and Autumn period ended, entering the Warring States era. Seven major states competed (Qin, Chu, Yan, Han, Zhao, Wei, Qi), with warfare escalating. This period saw the flourishing of the Hundred Schools of Thought, including Confucianism, Taoism, Legalism, and Mohism.

events.title: Qin Unification of China
events.description: King Ying Zheng of Qin conquered the six states, unified China, and proclaimed himself 'First Emperor' (Qin Shi Huang). He established centralized governance, standardized writing, currency, and weights/measures, and built the Great Wall. Though brief, the Qin laid China's unified political framework.

events.title: Great Wall Construction
events.description: Qin Shi Huang ordered General Meng Tian to lead 300,000 troops north against the Xiongnu, connecting and building the Great Wall to defend against northern nomads. The Great Wall became one of ancient China's greatest engineering feats and a symbol of Chinese civilization.

events.title: Death of Qin Shi Huang
events.description: Qin Shi Huang died at Shaqiu during his fifth imperial tour. After his death, Zhao Gao and Li Si altered his will, installing Huhai as Second Emperor, triggering political turmoil that led to the Qin Dynasty's rapid collapse.

events.title: Han Dynasty Founded
events.description: Liu Bang defeated Xiang Yu and established the Han Dynasty with Chang'an as capital. The Han inherited and improved Qin systems, implementing a dual commandery-kingdom system. Chinese culture flourished during this period, with 'Han people' and 'Chinese characters' deriving their names from this era.

events.title: Zhang Qian's Journey to the Western Regions
events.description: Emperor Wu dispatched Zhang Qian to seek alliance with the Yuezhi against the Xiongnu. Zhang's western expedition opened the Silk Road, promoting cultural and economic exchange between East and West, profoundly impacting world history.

events.title: Establishment of Imperial Academy
events.description: Emperor Wu adopted Dong Zhongshu's advice to 'dismiss the hundred schools, venerate only Confucianism,' establishing the Imperial Academy in Chang'an. It became China's highest learning institution, training officials, with Confucianism becoming state ideology.

events.title: Wang Mang Usurps the Han
events.description: Wang Mang, a powerful consort relative, usurped the Han throne and established the Xin Dynasty, implementing various reforms. However, the reforms failed, sparking peasant uprisings. The Xin lasted only 15 years before being overthrown by Liu Xiu.

events.title: Eastern Han Founded
events.description: Liu Xiu overthrew Wang Mang's regime, restored the Han, and established his capital in Luoyang, known as the Eastern Han. During this period, Buddhism entered China, papermaking was improved, and culture and arts flourished.

events.title: Cai Lun Improves Papermaking
events.description: Cai Lun, a Eastern Han eunuch, improved papermaking using tree bark, hemp, rags, and fishnets. The invention of paper was China's major contribution to world civilization, greatly promoting cultural dissemination.

events.title: Yellow Turban Rebellion
events.description: The Yellow Turban Rebellion led by Zhang Jue erupted, marking the beginning of late Eastern Han peasant wars. Though suppressed, the Eastern Han regime existed in name only, leading to warlord fragmentation and the Three Kingdoms era.

events.title: Three Kingdoms Era Begins
events.description: Cao Pi usurped the Han, establishing Wei, officially ending the Eastern Han. Subsequently, Liu Bei established Shu Han, and Sun Quan established Eastern Wu, forming the Three Kingdoms tripartite division. The period saw frequent warfare but continued cultural development.

events.title: Western Jin Unifies China
events.description: The Western Jin established by Sima Yan conquered Eastern Wu, ending the Three Kingdoms division and unifying the country. However, Western Jin was short-lived, with intense internal struggles, soon falling into the 'War of the Eight Princes.'

events.title: Five Barbarians Invade China
events.description: Western Jin fell, the north entered a century-long fragmentation known as 'Five Barbarians and Sixteen Kingdoms.' Large numbers of Han Chinese migrated south, promoting north-south cultural fusion. Buddhism spread widely in China during this period.

events.title: Northern Wei Founded
events.description: Tuoba Gui established Northern Wei, gradually unifying the north. Northern Wei implemented Sinicization reforms, promoting ethnic integration. Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital to Luoyang, pushing comprehensive Sinicization policies that profoundly impacted Chinese history.

events.title: Southern Dynasties Begin
events.description: Liu Yu established Song, beginning the Southern Dynasties (Song, Qi, Liang, Chen). The Southern Dynasties occupied the Jiangnan region, with flourishing culture and arts, achieving new heights in poetry, painting, and calligraphy.

events.title: Northern Wei Relocates to Luoyang
events.description: Emperor Xiaowen moved the capital from Pingcheng (modern Datong) to Luoyang, implementing comprehensive Sinicization reforms including adopting Han clothing, speaking Chinese, and using Han surnames. These reforms promoted great ethnic integration.

events.title: Sui Dynasty Founded
events.description: Yang Jian established the Sui Dynasty, conquering Southern Chen in 589 and ending nearly 300 years of north-south division. The Sui unified the country, established the imperial examination system, and built the Grand Canal, laying foundations for Tang prosperity.

events.title: Grand Canal Construction
events.description: Emperor Yang ordered construction of the Grand Canal, connecting the Yellow and Yangtze River basins. The canal, approximately 1,800 km long, became the world's longest canal, promoting north-south economic and cultural exchange with profound historical impact.

events.title: Tang Dynasty Founded
events.description: Li Yuan established the Tang Dynasty with Chang'an as capital. The Tang was one of China's most prosperous dynasties, with a flourishing economy, brilliant culture, and frequent foreign exchanges, hailed as China's ancient 'Golden Age.'

events.title: Xuanwu Gate Incident
events.description: Li Shimin launched the Xuanwu Gate coup, killing his brothers to seize the throne, becoming Emperor Taizong. He governed diligently, creating the 'Zhenguan Reign,' one of China's most famous golden ages.

events.title: Wu Zetian Becomes Emperor
events.description: Wu Zetian changed the dynasty name to Zhou, becoming China's only female emperor. During her reign, she continued promoting the imperial examination system, selecting talent, and promoting social development.

events.title: Kaiyuan Prosperity Begins
events.description: After Emperor Xuanzong's ascension, he governed diligently, creating the 'Kaiyuan Prosperity.' This period saw economic flourishing, brilliant culture, Chang'an becoming the world's largest city, and Tang power reaching its zenith.

events.title: An Lushan Rebellion
events.description: An Lushan and Shi Siming launched a rebellion, marking Tang's decline from prosperity. The rebellion lasted 8 years, causing massive population loss and severe economic destruction. Though eventually suppressed, Tang central authority was greatly weakened.

events.title: Huang Chao Rebellion
events.description: Huang Chao led a peasant uprising, capturing Chang'an and establishing the Great Qi regime. Though suppressed, the Tang central government existed in name only, with regional military governors gaining power, leading to Tang's demise.

events.title: Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms Begin
events.description: Zhu Wen destroyed Tang, establishing Later Liang, and China entered the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms fragmentation. Five Dynasties refers to northern Later Liang, Later Tang, Later Jin, Later Han, and Later Zhou; Ten Kingdoms to southern separatist regimes.

events.title: Song Dynasty Founded
events.description: Zhao Kuangyin launched the 'Chenqiao Mutiny' and established the Song Dynasty with Kaifeng as capital. The Song emphasized culture over military, perfected the civil service examination system, and achieved highly developed economy and culture, representing a pinnacle of ancient Chinese civilization.

events.title: Treaty of Chanyuan
events.description: Emperor Zhenzong signed the 'Treaty of Chanyuan' with Liao, with Song annually providing tribute in exchange for peace. This treaty established a century of Song-Liao peace but revealed Song's military weakness.

events.title: Bi Sheng Invents Movable Type
events.description: Bi Sheng of Northern Song invented movable type printing using ceramic characters for typesetting. Movable type printing was one of China's Four Great Inventions, making enormous contributions to world civilization dissemination.

events.title: Wang Anshi Reforms
events.description: Emperor Shenzong appointed Wang Anshi to implement New Policies, attempting fiscal and military reforms. The reforms faced fierce conservative opposition and ultimately failed. Reform controversies triggered factional strife, affecting late Northern Song politics.

events.title: Jingkang Incident
events.description: Jin forces breached Kaifeng, capturing Emperors Huizong and Qinzong, ending Northern Song. Emperor Gaozong Zhao Gou fled south, establishing the Southern Song regime in Lin'an (modern Hangzhou). The Jingkang Incident became a major disaster in Chinese history.

events.title: Genghis Khan Unifies Mongolia
events.description: Temüjin unified Mongol tribes, was proclaimed 'Genghis Khan,' and established the Great Mongol State. Mongol cavalry began westward conquests, building a vast empire spanning Eurasia.

events.title: Mongols Destroy Jin
events.description: Mongol and Southern Song allied forces destroyed Jin. After Jin's fall, Mongols turned south to attack Southern Song, opening the conquest of Song.

events.title: Yuan Dynasty Established
events.description: Kublai Khan changed the nation's name to 'Great Yuan,' formally establishing the Yuan Dynasty. The Yuan was China's first nationwide regime established by an ethnic minority, with unprecedented territorial expanse.

events.title: Yuan Unifies China
events.description: Yuan forces defeated Southern Song remnants at the Battle of Yamen, ending Southern Song and unifying China. Lu Xiufu carried young Emperor Zhao Bing into the sea in a tragic moment in Chinese history.

events.title: Ming Dynasty Founded
events.description: Zhu Yuanzhang overthrew the Yuan and established the Ming Dynasty with Nanjing as capital. The Ming restored Han Chinese rule, implemented centralized governance, abolished the prime minister position, and strengthened imperial power. The period saw economic prosperity and cultural development.

events.title: Zheng He's Voyages
events.description: Emperor Yongle dispatched Zheng He to lead massive fleets on seven voyages, reaching as far as East Africa. These expeditions demonstrated Ming's power and promoted maritime trade and cultural exchange.

events.title: Capital Moved to Beijing
events.description: Emperor Yongle moved the capital from Nanjing to Beijing, massively constructing Beijing city including the Forbidden City and Temple of Heaven. Beijing became China's political center, a status continuing to this day.

events.title: Tumu Crisis
events.description: Emperor Yingzong personally campaigned against the Oirat, was captured at Tumu. This event marked Ming's decline from prosperity; thereafter northern border pressure increased and internal political struggles intensified.

events.title: Portuguese Arrive in China
events.description: Portuguese envoys reached Guangzhou, marking the first European colonizers to reach China. Subsequently, Western missionaries and merchants came to China, increasing Sino-Western cultural exchange.

events.title: Matteo Ricci Arrives in China
events.description: Italian Jesuit Matteo Ricci came to China, spreading Western scientific knowledge and Catholicism. Ricci mastered Chinese, compiled the 'Complete Map of the Myriad Countries,' promoting Sino-Western cultural exchange.

events.title: Qing Dynasty Entry into China
events.description: Li Zicheng captured Beijing, ending the Ming Dynasty. Ming general Wu Sangui invited Qing forces through the pass, establishing Qing rule over all China. The Manchu Qing ruled for nearly 300 years as China's last feudal dynasty.

events.title: Kangxi Emperor Ascends
events.description: The Kangxi Emperor ascended, inaugurating the 'Kangxi-Qianlong Prosperity.' Kangxi reigned 61 years, suppressing the Three Feudatories, recovering Taiwan, defeating the Dzungars, and consolidating the unified multi-ethnic state.

events.title: Recovery of Taiwan
events.description: Qing forces captured Taiwan, the Zheng regime surrendered. The Qing established Taiwan Prefecture under Fujian Province, strengthening Taiwan administration.

events.title: Treaty of Nerchinsk Signed
events.description: The Qing signed the Treaty of Nerchinsk with Russia, delimiting the eastern Sino-Russian border. This was China's first equal treaty with a Western nation.

events.title: Yongzheng Emperor Ascends
events.description: The Yongzheng Emperor implemented various reforms including integrating poll tax into land tax and the palace memorial system, strengthening centralization and improving administrative efficiency.

events.title: Qianlong Emperor Ascends
events.description: The Qianlong Emperor ascended, with Qing power reaching its zenith. The Qianlong era saw vast territory and economic prosperity, but also signs of decline, with serious bureaucratic corruption.

events.title: Macartney Embassy to China
events.description: Britain dispatched the Macartney Embassy to visit the Qing, requesting trade. The Qianlong Emperor refused British demands, deteriorating Sino-British relations and foreshadowing the later Opium Wars.

events.title: Destruction of Opium at Humen
events.description: Lin Zexu destroyed opium at Humen in Guangzhou, demonstrating the Qing government's determination to ban opium. This act angered Britain, becoming a trigger for the Opium War.

events.title: First Opium War
events.description: Britain launched the Opium War; Qing forces were defeated. The 1842 Treaty of Nanjing ceded Hong Kong and opened five treaty ports, beginning China's descent into semi-colonial, semi-feudal status.

events.title: Taiping Rebellion
events.description: Hong Xiuquan launched the Taiping Rebellion, establishing the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom with Nanjing as capital. The movement lasted 14 years, sweeping half of China, becoming the largest peasant uprising in Chinese history.

events.title: Second Opium War
events.description: Anglo-French forces launched the Second Opium War, capturing Beijing in 1860 and burning the Old Summer Palace. The Qing government was forced to sign a series of unequal treaties, losing more sovereignty.

events.title: Self-Strengthening Movement Begins
events.description: Amid internal troubles and foreign aggression, the Qing launched the Self-Strengthening Movement with slogans of 'self-strengthening' and 'seeking wealth,' establishing military and civilian enterprises, sending students abroad, attempting to achieve wealth and power.

events.title: First Sino-Japanese War
events.description: The First Sino-Japanese War erupted, with Qing forces suffering catastrophic defeat. The 1895 Treaty of Shimonoseki ceded Taiwan and Penghu, with 200 million taels indemnity, causing China's international status to plummet.

events.title: Hundred Days' Reform
events.description: Emperor Guangxu supported Kang Youwei and Liang Qichao in implementing reform, attempting political reforms. However, the reform lasted only 103 days before being overthrown by Empress Dowager Cixi's coup.

events.title: Boxer Rebellion and Eight-Nation Alliance
events.description: The Boxer Rebellion arose, opposing foreign aggression. The Eight-Nation Alliance invaded China, capturing Beijing. The 1901 Boxer Protocol signed, making China completely semi-colonial.

events.title: Abolition of Imperial Examinations
events.description: The Qing government announced abolition of the 1,300-year imperial examination system, establishing new-style schools. Examination abolition marked the end of traditional education and the beginning of modern education.

events.title: Xinhai Revolution
events.description: The Wuchang Uprising erupted, rapidly spreading nationwide. The Qing emperor abdicated in 1912, ending over two millennia of imperial rule. The Republic of China was established with Sun Yat-sen as provisional president.

events.title: New Culture Movement
events.description: Chen Duxiu founded 'New Youth' magazine in Shanghai, advocating democracy and science, criticizing Confucian tradition. The New Culture Movement profoundly influenced Chinese thought and culture.

events.title: May Fourth Movement
events.description: China's diplomatic failure at the Paris Peace Conference sparked the May Fourth Movement. Students demonstrated with the slogan 'External resistance to foreign powers, internal punishment of traitors.' This marked the beginning of China's New Democratic Revolution.

events.title: Founding of the Communist Party of China
events.description: The First National Congress of the Communist Party of China convened in Shanghai, announcing the Party's establishment. This was an epoch-making event in Chinese history.

events.title: Nanchang Uprising
events.description: The Communist Party launched the Nanchang Uprising, firing the first shot of armed resistance against the Nationalists. August 1 became People's Liberation Army Day.

events.title: Mukden Incident
events.description: Japan's Kwantung Army launched the Mukden Incident, occupying the three northeastern provinces. Japan established the puppet state of Manchukuo in the northeast, intensifying Sino-Japanese ethnic conflict.

events.title: Long March Begins
events.description: The Central Red Army was forced into strategic retreat, beginning the Long March. The Red Army endured hardships, traveling 25,000 li, finally reaching northern Shaanxi. The Long March became a magnificent epic of the Chinese Revolution.

events.title: Marco Polo Bridge Incident
events.description: Japan launched full-scale invasion of China with the Marco Polo Bridge Incident. The Second United Front was formed between the Nationalists and Communists to resist Japan. The Chinese people began eight arduous years of war.

events.title: Victory in War of Resistance Against Japan
events.description: Japan announced unconditional surrender, China's War of Resistance against Japan victorious. As a victor nation, China recovered Taiwan and other lost territories, with elevated international status.

events.title: Founding of the People's Republic of China
events.description: On October 1, Mao Zedong proclaimed the founding of the People's Republic of China at Tiananmen in Beijing. The Chinese people had stood up, beginning a new era of socialist construction.

events.title: Land Reform
events.description: Nationwide land reform movement launched, abolishing feudal land ownership, achieving 'land to the tiller.' Land reform liberated rural productivity and consolidated the new regime.

events.title: First Five-Year Plan
events.description: China began implementing the First Five-Year Plan, focusing on heavy industry development and establishing an industrialization foundation. The Soviet Union provided substantial aid, with 156 key projects progressively launched.

events.title: First Constitution Promulgated
events.description: The First National People's Congress adopted the 'Constitution of the People's Republic of China,' establishing the people's congress system. This was New China's first socialist-type constitution.

events.title: Great Leap Forward
events.description: The 'Great Leap Forward' movement launched, attempting to rapidly achieve industrialization. However, violating economic laws, it caused severe economic difficulties and famine.

events.title: First Atomic Bomb Successfully Tested
events.description: China's first atomic bomb successfully tested at Lop Nur in Xinjiang, breaking superpower nuclear monopoly. China became the world's fifth nuclear weapons state.

events.title: First Satellite Launched
events.description: China's first artificial Earth satellite 'Dongfanghong 1' successfully launched. China became the world's fifth country capable of independently launching satellites.

events.title: Return to United Nations
events.description: The UN General Assembly passed a resolution restoring the People's Republic of China's lawful seat in the United Nations. China's international status significantly elevated.

events.title: Nixon Visits China
events.description: US President Nixon visited China, beginning Sino-American rapprochement. The Shanghai Communiqué's publication marked the start of Sino-American normalization.

events.title: Reform and Opening Up
events.description: The Third Plenum of the 11th CPC Central Committee convened, establishing reform and opening-up policies. China embarked on a market economy path, experiencing earth-shaking economic and social changes.

events.title: Sino-American Diplomatic Relations Established
events.description: The People's Republic of China and United States formally established diplomatic relations. Sino-American relations had major impact on the international landscape.

events.title: Special Economic Zones Established
events.description: Established Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Shantou, and Xiamen as four special economic zones implementing special economic policies. SEZs became windows and testing grounds for reform and opening up.

events.title: Household Responsibility System
events.description: Rural areas widely implemented the household contract responsibility system, greatly mobilizing farmers' enthusiasm. Agricultural productivity was liberated, rural economy rapidly developed.

events.title: Coastal Cities Opened
events.description: Further opened 14 coastal cities, expanding opening-up scope. Coastal regions became engines of China's economic development.

events.title: Deng Xiaoping's Southern Tour
events.description: Deng Xiaoping's southern tour and important speeches pushed reform and opening into a new stage. The 14th Party Congress established the goal of building a socialist market economy system.

events.title: Hong Kong's Return
events.description: On July 1, the Chinese government resumed sovereignty over Hong Kong. This historic moment washed away a century of humiliation, successfully implementing the 'one country, two systems' concept.

events.title: Macao's Return
events.description: On December 20, the Chinese government resumed sovereignty over Macao. Macao's return marked the disappearance of the last colonial territory on Chinese soil.

events.title: WTO Accession
events.description: China formally joined the World Trade Organization (WTO), integrating into globalization. China's economy rapidly took off, becoming the 'world's factory.'

events.title: Manned Spaceflight Success
events.description: Shenzhou 5 manned spacecraft successfully launched, Yang Liwei became China's first astronaut. China became the world's third country to master manned spaceflight technology.

events.title: Beijing Olympics
events.description: Beijing successfully hosted the 29th Summer Olympic Games, showcasing China's comprehensive national strength and positive international image. The Wenchuan earthquake also occurred this year, with the nation united in disaster relief.

events.title: Became World's Second Largest Economy
events.description: China's GDP surpassed Japan, becoming the world's second largest economy. China's economic aggregate continued to rise as a global percentage.

events.title: Belt and Road Initiative
events.description: Proposed the 'Belt and Road Initiative,' promoting economic cooperation with countries along the routes. This initiative became an important platform for China's opening up and international cooperation.

events.title: Two-Child Policy Fully Implemented
events.description: The comprehensive two-child policy officially implemented, adjusting population policy to address aging challenges. This marked the complete end of the 30-plus year one-child policy.

events.title: New Era Inaugurated
events.description: The 19th Party Congress convened, announcing socialism with Chinese characteristics entered a new era. Proposed the 'two centenary goals' and the Chinese Dream of national rejuvenation.

events.title: Complete Victory in Poverty Alleviation
events.description: Completed poverty alleviation tasks, eliminating absolute poverty. Nearly 100 million rural poor achieved poverty alleviation, creating a miracle in human poverty reduction history.

events.title: Fighting COVID-19 Pandemic
events.description: The COVID-19 pandemic broke out, China adopted strict prevention measures, controlling the epidemic spread in a relatively short time. Wuhan locked down for 76 days, the entire nation united against the epidemic.

events.title: CPC Centenary
events.description: Celebrating the 100th anniversary of the Communist Party of China, announcing the completion of building a moderately prosperous society. China achieved its first centenary goal, embarking on a new journey of comprehensive socialist modernization.

events.title: Beijing Winter Olympics
events.description: Beijing successfully hosted the 24th Winter Olympic Games, becoming the first city to host both Summer and Winter Olympics, a 'Double Olympic City.'

events.title: Economic Recovery and Development
events.description: After optimizing pandemic prevention policies, China's economy gradually recovered. Continued to promote high-quality development, strengthen scientific and technological innovation, and advance industrial upgrading.
